tasks.title: Prove transferOperatorBounded and transferOperator_series→CLM assembly in lean/Riemann/TransferOperator/Operator.lean (kill the 2 remaining sorries). Read lean/PROOF_TASKS_BRIEF.md first. NEVER modify lean/lake-manifest.json, lean/lean-toolchain or lean/lakefile.lean — the build environment is pre-seeded; if lake build is slow, just wait. Strategy: define (L_s f) x = tsum of transferOperatorSummand s f n x; each summand is continuous in x (Complex.continuousAt_cpow at nonzero base + composition), the series converges uniformly on Set.Icc 0 1 by Weierstrass M-test with x-free bound ‖f‖ * ((n:ℝ)+1)^(-2*s.re) (use inverse_pow_monotone_x and Real.summable_nat_rpow + summable_nat_add_iff, both already proven in BasicProofs.lean); tsum of continuous functions is continuous via Summable.of_norm in the Banach space C(Set.Icc 0 1, ℂ); linearity from tsum commutation with evaluation (ContinuousLinearMap.map_tsum or hasSum_apply); assemble the ContinuousLinearMap via LinearMap.mkContinuous with bound C = (∑' n, (n+1)^(-2*re s)) * ‖f‖ or via tsum-based operator norm. Grep .lake/packages/mathlib for exact names: continuousAt_cpow, M-test lemmas (tendstoUniformly, hasSum), LinearMap.mkContinuous.

These are elementary real-analysis facts: continuity of x ↦ 1/(n+1+x) on x>0 (Continuous.inv_ones or Continuous.div with positivity), continuity of fract of 1/x minus floor away from discontinuities, contraction |I x - I y| = |x-y|/((n+1+x)(n+1+y)) ≤ |x-y|/4 (linarith/ring + div_le_div), monotone bijection [0,1] → [1/(n+2), 1/(n+1)] (Monotone + surjectivity via intermediate value or explicit inverse). tasks.title: Prove riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_re_eq_one in lean/Riemann/PrimeNumberTheorem.lean (Fleet 6 line theorem: riemannZeta s ≠ 0 for Re s = 1, s ≠ 1). Read lean/PROOF_TASKS_BRIEF.md first. NEVER modify lean/lake-manifest.json, lean/lean-toolchain or lean/lakefile.lean — the build environment is pre-seeded; if lake build is slow, just wait. This is the classical Hadamard–de la Vallée Poussin consequence: ζ(s) ≠ 0 on Re s = 1 (s ≠ 1) follows from the non-vanishing of ζ on Re s > 1 and the functional equation / Hadamard product theory, OR from the classical 3-point argument via (1 - 2^{1-s}) ζ(s) = ζ Dirichlet eta relation. Mathlib may already have: grep for riemannZeta ne_zero, RiemannZeta.s_ne_zero, Analysis.RiemannZeta — Mathlib.Mathlib.NumberTheory.RiemannZeta has s_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re or similar; also check Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries. If Mathlib has the statement for Re s > 1 only, combine with zeta_reflect (already in the file) and continuity/analytic continuation (riemannZeta_analytic / DifferentiableOn) + identity theorem to push to the line Re s = 1. If truly missing in Mathlib, prove the line theorem via the eta-function limit argument. IMPORTANT: do not introduce axioms; if a substep is out of reach, split it into a documented sorry-lemma ONLY for that substep and explain in the commit message.
